{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Free public higher education would take what should be a universal public good out of the marketplace, put it under democratic control, and guarantee it as a right to all citizens.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Free public higher education would be funded by a truly progressive tax system that makes the wealthy and corporations pay their fair share of government revenue.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A campaign for free public higher education would show people that socialist policies are both desirable and achievable.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Gaining free public higher education could serve as a crucial step in making democratic socialist politics more attractive to a wider cross-section of the U.S. public.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Achieving goals will require grassroots organizing and “street heat”.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Achieving goals will require a critical mass of political office holders to implement them.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Elections in and of themselves will not bring about major political, economic or social reforms, nor establish a pathway to socialism.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"It is difficult to imagine achieving objectives in the United States without taking part in the electoral process.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
